{{Short description|Canadian writer, filmmaker, and environmentalist (born 1970)}}
{{Infobox person
| name          = Frank Wolf
| image         = Frank_Wolf.jpg
| image_caption = Frank Wolf during the ''Maze of the North'' expedition
| birth_date    = {{Birth year and age|1970}}
| occupation    = [[Adventurer]], writer, filmmaker, environmentalist

'''Frank Wolf''' (born 1970) is a Canadian [[adventurer]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Explore Magazine profile|url=http://explore-mag.com/4077/adventure/frank-wolf-environmental-expeditoneer|access-date=2012-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019063121/http://explore-mag.com/4077/adventure/frank-wolf-environmental-expeditoneer|archive-date=2013-10-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> writer,<ref name="auto3">{{cite book|title=Lines on a Map book on Amazon Canada|id={{ASIN|1771602899|country=ca}} }}</ref> filmmaker,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imdb.com/name/nm2526253/|title=Frank Wolf|website=IMDb|access-date=2012-11-09|archive-date=2012-06-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120611073508/http://www.imdb.com/name/nm2526253/|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[environmentalist]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.canoekayak.com/travel/wilderness-protection-canada/#STYoOcJlIHTwSYkj.97|title=Canoe & Kayak Magazine profile|access-date=2015-10-01|archive-date=2015-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004110027/http://www.canoekayak.com/travel/wilderness-protection-canada/#STYoOcJlIHTwSYkj.97|url-status=live}}</ref> He is known for books, feature magazine articles, online columns, and films that document wilderness expeditions around the world, with a focus on the Canadian North.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.midwesterngentleman.com/people/frank-wolf-wild-one/|title=Midwestern Gentleman Magazine profile|access-date=2016-03-16|archive-date=2016-03-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321104708/http://www.midwesterngentleman.com/people/frank-wolf-wild-one/|url-status=live}}</ref> His expeditions include being the first to canoe across Canada in one season and cycling 2,000&nbsp;km in winter on the Yukon River from Dawson to Nome. In 2020 he was named One of Canada's Greatest 90 Explorers of All Time by ''[[Canadian Geographic]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.canadiangeographic.ca/article/canadas-90-greatest-explorers-crucial-communication|title=Canada's 90 Greatest Explorers of All Time|website=Canadian Geographic|access-date=2021-04-13|archive-date=2021-04-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413173153/https://www.canadiangeographic.ca/article/canadas-90-greatest-explorers-crucial-communication|url-status=live}}</ref> and in 2012 he was named one of Canada's Top Ten Adventurers by [[explore (magazine)|''Explore'']].<ref>{{cite web|title=Explore Magazine Top 10 Adventurers|url=http://explore-mag.com/4077/adventure/frank-wolf-environmental-expeditoneer|access-date=2012-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019063121/http://explore-mag.com/4077/adventure/frank-wolf-environmental-expeditoneer|archive-date=2013-10-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has written two books on his adventures: ''Two Springs, One Summer'' (2024) and ''[[Lines on a Map]]'' (2018), both published by RMB.<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://rmbooks.com/products/two-springs-one-summer|title= Two Springs, One Summer}}</ref><ref name="auto3"/><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://rmbooks.com/book/lines-on-a-map/|title=Lines on a Map|website=Rocky Mountain Books|access-date=2018-08-17|archive-date=2018-08-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817193431/https://rmbooks.com/book/lines-on-a-map/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Lines on a Map book on Amazon.com|isbn=1771602899 }}</ref> His films include ''Wild Ones'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vimeo.com/139800872|title=Wild Ones film trailer|access-date=2017-08-30|archive-date=2017-02-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170201113105/https://vimeo.com/139800872|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The Hand of Franklin]]'', ''[[Kitturiaq]]'', [[On the Line (2011 film)|''On the Line'']], ''[[Mammalian (film)|Mammalian]]'', and ''[[Borealis (2008 film)|Borealis]]'', all of which broadcast on CBC's [[Documentary Channel (Canada)|Documentary Channel]] in Canada.<ref>{{cite news|title=On The Line on CBC's documentary channel|url=http://www.cbc.ca/programguide/program/on_the_line/|work=CBC News|access-date=2012-12-28|archive-date=2013-10-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021084105/http://www.cbc.ca/programguide/program/on_the_line/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Expeditions==
[[File:Frank Wolf Expeditions Map.jpg|thumb|A map of Frank Wolf's self-propelled wilderness expeditions in North America]]Map of Frank Wolf's self-propelled expeditions in North America

* (2026) ''Nèhtrùh Expedition'': 21-day, 1,200 km canoe journey from [[Elliot Lake, Yukon|Elliot Lake]], to [[Old Crow, Yukon|Old Crow]] with Alex Kozma<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://explorersweb.com/on-the-trail-of-the-mad-trapper-paddling-1200km-through-canada/|title= On the Trail of the Mad Trapper}}</ref>
* (2025) ''Deh Cho Solo Expedition'': 21-day, 1,620&nbsp;km solo kayak journey down the length of the [[Mackenzie River]], from [[Hay River, Northwest Territories|Hay River]] to [[Inuvik]]<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.instagram.com/p/DNizM-Hxo9e/?ref=badge&img_index=1/|title= Deh Cho Solo}}</ref>
* (2025) ''Taan Expedition'': 25-day, 720&nbsp;km kayak journey through the [[Alaskan Panhandle]], in the month of May, starting from and returning to [[Prince Rupert, British Columbia|Prince Rupert]], with Dave Berrisford <ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.instagram.com/p/DKfCNu2x5rT/?ref=badge&img_index=1/|title= Taan Expedition}}</ref>
* (2024) ''Yamozha Expedition'': 36-day, 1,350&nbsp;km canoe journey from [[Yellowknife]] to [[Kugluqtuk]] via the [[Yellowknife River]], [[Starvation River]], [[Rockinghorse Lake]], [[Hood River (Nunavut)|Hood River]], and the [[Northwest Passage]] with Arturo Simondetti <ref>{{Cite web |url= https://explorersweb.com/wandering-1400km-to-the-northwest-passage/|title= Wandering 1,400 km to the Northwest Passage}}</ref>
* (2024) ''Kangiqluk Expedition'': 18-day, 325&nbsp;km ski journey in the [[Clyde River (Baffin Island)|Clyde River]] region of [[Baffin Island]] with Dave Garrow and John McClelland <ref>{{Cite web |url= https://explorersweb.com/arctic-roundup-spring-season-ends-with-a-flurry/|title= Spring Season Ends with a Flurry }}</ref>
* (2024) ''Round the Gap Expedition'': 19-day, 500&nbsp;km kayak journey from [[Colón, Panama|Colon]], [[Panama]] to [[Turbocharger|Turbo]], [[Colombia]] around the [[Darién Gap]] with Mark Sky <ref>{{Cite web |url= https://paddlingmag.com/stories/columns/fathom/darien-gap/|title= Frank Wolf Rounds the Darien Gap }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url= https://explore-mag.com/the-way-of-the-wolf-kayaking-round-the-gap// |title= Explore Mag, Kayaking Round the Gap }}</ref> 
* (2023) ''Tongait Expedition'': 27-day, 920&nbsp;km kayak journey via [[Ungava Bay]] and the [[Labrador Sea]] from [[Kangiqsualujjuaq]], to [[Nain, Newfoundland and Labrador|Nain]], with Justine Curgenven, JF Marleau, and Larry Chomyn <ref>{{Cite web |url= https://kokatat.com/blog/tongait-expedition |title= Tongait Expedition }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url= https://explorersweb.com/kayakers-polar-bears-labrador/ |title= Explorer's Web }}</ref> 
* (2023) ''Laxmoon Expedition '': Solo 14-day, 400&nbsp;km kayak journey along the north coast of [[British Columbia]] via [[Porcher Island]], [[Banks Island]], [[Campania Island]] and [[Price Island]] from [[Prince Rupert, British Columbia|Prince Rupert]] to [[Bella Bella, British Columbia|Bella Bella]]<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://kokatat.com/blog/laxmoon-expedition-photo-essay |title= Laxmoon Photo essay }}</ref> 
* (2022) ''Goba Expedition '': 30-day, 1300&nbsp;km canoe journey from the Yukon/NWT border to [[Kugluktuk]] via the [[Tsichu River]], [[Keele River]], [[Great Bear River]], [[Great Bear Lake]], [[Sloane River]], [[Hook River]] and [[Coppermine River]] with Alex Kozma.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://kokatat.com/blog/the-goba-expedition|title= Goba Expedition photo essay|website= Kokatat}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://paddlingmag.com/stories/columns/canvas/arctic-expedition/|title= Padling Magazine Canvas article|website= Paddling Magazine}}</ref> 
* (2022) ''Pikialasorsuaq Expedition '': 20-day, 300&nbsp;km ski journey along the [[North Water Polynya]], over the [[Devon Ice Cap]], and across [[Jones Sound]] to finish at [[Grise Fiord]] on [[Ellesmere Island]], with Dave Garrow and John McClelland.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://polarbearsinternational.org/news-media/articles/north-water-polynya-expedition/|title= Pikialasorsuaq Expedition|website= Polar Bears International|access-date= 2022-09-19|archive-date= 2022-09-20|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220920171147/https://polarbearsinternational.org/news-media/articles/north-water-polynya-expedition/|url-status= live}}</ref> 
* (2021) ''Sa Tu Expedition'': 30-day, 1360&nbsp;km canoe circuit along the [[Athabasca River]], [[Lake Athabasca]], Fond Du Lac River, Cree River, [[Cree Lake]], Black Birch Lake, Careen Lake, and [[Clearwater River (Alberta)|Clearwater River]] starting and finishing in [[Fort McMurray]], with Dave Greene.<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://kokatat.com/blog/sa-tu-expedition |title= Sa Tu Expedition |website= Kokatat |access-date= 2021-12-07 |archive-date= 2021-12-07 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211207175746/https://kokatat.com/blog/sa-tu-expedition |url-status= live }}</ref> 
* (2021) ''Qwunus Expedition'': 38-day, 1320&nbsp;km kayak journey circumnavigating [[Vancouver Island]], starting and finishing in [[West Vancouver]], with Dave Berrisford and Amber Blenkiron.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kokatat.com/blog/qwunus-expedition|title=Qwunus Expedition|website=kokatat|access-date=2021-08-12|archive-date=2021-08-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812215242/https://kokatat.com/blog/qwunus-expedition|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url= https://issuu.com/mountainlifemedia/docs/mlcm-summer-2022/102 |title= Symbiosis |website= Kokatat |access-date= 2022-09-19 |archive-date= 2022-09-20 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220920172642/https://issuu.com/mountainlifemedia/docs/mlcm-summer-2022/102 |url-status= live }}</ref>
* (2020) ''Sine Tanize Expedition'' : 25-day, 1060&nbsp;km canoe expedition through [[Manitoba]] from [[Sandy Bay First Nation]] to [[Hudson Bay]], via the [[Churchill River (Hudson Bay)|Churchill River]], [[Barrington River (Manitoba)|Barrington River]], and [[Seal River (Manitoba)|Seal River]] with Shauna Liora.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kokatat.com/blog/sine-tanize-canoe-expedition|title=Sine Tanize Expedition Photo Essay|website=Kokatat|access-date=2021-03-31|archive-date=2021-02-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228135506/https://kokatat.com/blog/sine-tanize-canoe-expedition|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2020) ''The Bear and the Wolf Paddle North'' : 27-day, 1000&nbsp;km sea kayak expedition along the west coast of [[British Columbia]] from [[Squamish, British Columbia|Squamish]] to [[Prince Rupert, British Columbia|Prince Rupert]], with Dave Berrisford.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kokatat.com/blog/the-bear-and-the-wolf-paddle-north|title=The Bear and the Wolf Paddle North|website=Kokatat|access-date=2020-08-18|archive-date=2021-05-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518174504/https://kokatat.com/blog/the-bear-and-the-wolf-paddle-north|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2019) ''The Lakeland Traverse'' : 20-day, 800&nbsp;km canoe expedition through [[Finland]] from [[Nurmes]] to [[Helsinki]], with Todd McGowan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://paddlingmag.com/trips/trip-reports/canoeing-in-finland/|title=Canoeing Saunaland|website=Paddling Magazine|date=6 November 2020|access-date=9 June 2021|archive-date=9 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210609192813/https://paddlingmag.com/trips/trip-reports/canoeing-in-finland/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Way-of-the-Wolf-Canoeing-Saunaland|title=Canoeing Saunaland|website=Explore Magazine|access-date=2019-10-03|archive-date=2019-10-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191003213621/https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Way-of-the-Wolf-Canoeing-Saunaland|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Way-of-the-Wolf-A-Fine-Finnish|title=A Fine Finnish|website=Explore Magazine|access-date=2019-10-03|archive-date=2019-10-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191003213622/https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Way-of-the-Wolf-A-Fine-Finnish|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2019) ''Arctic Return'' : 18-day, 350&nbsp;km ski expedition from [[Naujaat]] to [[Pelly Bay]], with David Reid and Richard Smith. Reid and Smith continued on for another 200&nbsp;km to Rae Strait after Wolf had to abandon the journey due to injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.arcteryx.com/on-raes-trail|title=On Rae's Trail|website=Arcteryx|date=20 December 2019|access-date=9 June 2021|archive-date=23 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210623181035/https://blog.arcteryx.com/on-raes-trail/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mountainculturegroup.com/expedition-for-scottish-explorer-john-rae|title=Charles Dickens had him shunned|website=Coast Mountain Culture|date=7 January 2020|access-date=9 June 2021|archive-date=9 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210609192003/https://mountainculturegroup.com/expedition-for-scottish-explorer-john-rae/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2018) ''Baffin Ski Traverse'' : 14-day, 230&nbsp;km ski expedition across [[Baffin Island]] via the [[Penny Ice Cap]], with Dave Garrow and John McClelland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.arcteryx.com/the-land-that-never-melts/|title=Ski touring through the Land That Never Melts|first=A. Photo Essay From Frank Wolf's 230km Ski Tour Across Baffin|last=Isl|date=August 15, 2018|website=The Bird Blog - Arc'teryx|access-date=August 17, 2018|archive-date=August 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817225443/https://blog.arcteryx.com/the-land-that-never-melts/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Mckenzie">{{Cite web|url=https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Way-of-the-Wolf-Gearing-up-for-an-Arctic-Spring-Tour|title=Explore Magazine|first=Kevin Hinton & Ryan|last=Mckenzie|website=Explore Magazine|access-date=2018-06-21|archive-date=2018-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621194313/https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Way-of-the-Wolf-Gearing-up-for-an-Arctic-Spring-Tour|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2018) ''Across the Barrens'' : 35-day, 1750&nbsp;km canoe expedition from [[Yellowknife]] to the [[Arctic Ocean]] via [[Great Slave Lake]], Pike's Portage, and the [[Back River (Nunavut)|Back River]] with Ryan Bougie.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paddlers embraced by elders after 35-day journey|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/frank-wolf-paddle-northwest-territories-nunavut-1.4781476|access-date=2018-08-12|archive-date=2018-08-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812114620/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/frank-wolf-paddle-northwest-territories-nunavut-1.4781476|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Curious wolf on Back River campsite|url=http://www.cbc.ca/player/play/1296704579828|access-date=2018-08-11|archive-date=2023-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423171723/https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/1296704579828|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2017) ''Maze of the North Expedition'' : 30-day, 1350&nbsp;km canoe expedition from [[Pekans River]] bridge on [[Quebec Route 389]] to [[Umiujaq]], [[Quebec]] with Peirson Ross Mclean.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/mazeofthenorth/|title=Maze of the North Expedition|website=www.facebook.com|access-date=2017-08-30|archive-date=2023-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423171740/https://www.facebook.com/login/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fmazeofthenorth%2F|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2017) ''Angilaaq Mountain Expedition'' : 12-day, 160&nbsp;km ski expedition on [[Bylot Island]] to summit [[Angilaaq Mountain]], its highest peak, as well as 4 other sub-peaks, with Dave Garrow.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.arcteryx.com/methuselah-ancients-bylot/|title=Methuselah and the Ancients of Bylot|date=December 20, 2017|website=The Bird Blog - Arc'teryx|access-date=August 27, 2020|archive-date=August 11, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811031502/https://blog.arcteryx.com/methuselah-ancients-bylot/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= Images from Angilaaq summit images|url= https://twitter.com/frankwolf1/status/869280754588467200|access-date= 2017-08-30|archive-date= 2022-08-26|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220826032806/https://twitter.com/frankwolf1/status/869280754588467200|url-status= live}}</ref>
* (2016) ''Maskwa Nanook Expedition'' : 44-day, 1800&nbsp;km canoe journey from [[La Ronge]], [[Saskatchewan]] to [[Baker Lake, Nunavut]], with Shawn Campbell.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.canadiangeographic.ca/article/canoe-expedition-travelling-1600-km-saskatchewan-nunavut|title=Canoe expedition travelling 1600 km from Saskatchewan to Nunavut|date=July 25, 2016|website=Canadian Geographic|access-date=August 27, 2020|archive-date=July 7, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707170440/http://www.canadiangeographic.ca/article/canoe-expedition-travelling-1600-km-saskatchewan-nunavut|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2015) ''Spatsizi/Stikine Expedition'' : 9-day, 280&nbsp;km pack rafting/hiking route through the Spatsizi/Stikine Wilderness with Shawn Campbell.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/frankwolf/albums/72157657548886412|title=Expedition Album}}</ref>
* (2015) ''Wild Ones Music Tour'': 24-day, 750&nbsp;km concert tour by canoe from [[Parry Sound]] to [[Ottawa]]- with musician Peirson Ross.<ref>{{cite web|title= CBC's 'As it Happens' Interview|url= http://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-friday-edition-1.3111142/musician-peirson-ross-tours-latest-album-by-canoe-1.3111153|access-date= 2015-07-22|archive-date= 2015-07-11|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150711222126/http://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-friday-edition-1.3111142/musician-peirson-ross-tours-latest-album-by-canoe-1.3111153|url-status= live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://saveurfilms.wixsite.com/wild-ones|title=HOME|website=wild-ones|access-date=2020-08-27|archive-date=2020-04-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200408071826/https://saveurfilms.wixsite.com/wild-ones|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Happy-Camper-Reviewing-Frank-Wolfs-Wild-Ones|title=Explore Magazine|first=Kevin Hinton & Ryan|last=Mckenzie|website=Explore Magazine|access-date=2020-08-27|archive-date=2018-01-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119175558/https://www.explore-mag.com/The-Happy-Camper-Reviewing-Frank-Wolfs-Wild-Ones|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2015) ''Mammal Ski Survey'' : 7-day, 110&nbsp;km ski traverse with biologist tracking and logging large mammals in [[Banff National Park]]- with Dave Garrow and Ross Glenfield.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/frank.wolf.3914/posts/10153229981401319|title=Frank Wolf|website=www.facebook.com|access-date=2016-01-27|archive-date=2023-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423171726/https://www.facebook.com/login/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Ffrank.wolf.3914%2Fposts%2F10153229981401319|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2014) ''Sweetwater Soul'' : 26-day, 1350&nbsp;km journey by canoe from [[Pine Dock]], MB to [[Fort Severn]], ON- with Rob Hart.<ref>{{cite web|title= Sandy Lake First Nation article|url= http://sandylake.firstnation.ca/canoe-paddlers-stop-sandy-lake-way-fort-severn|access-date= 2014-08-20|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140821102112/http://sandylake.firstnation.ca/canoe-paddlers-stop-sandy-lake-way-fort-severn|archive-date= 2014-08-21|url-status= dead}}</ref>
* (2013) ''Mainstream Last First'' : 55-day, 1870&nbsp;km journey by rowboat through [[Northwest Passage]] from [[Inuvik]] to [[Cambridge Bay]], with Kevin Vallely, Paul Gleeson, Denis Barnett.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mainstreamlastfirst.com/|title=Mainstream Last First|website=mainstreamlastfirst.com|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-07-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130723013654/http://mainstreamlastfirst.com/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2012) ''Kitturiaq'' : 21-day, 620&nbsp;km first-ever journey by [[canoe]] over the [[Labrador]] Plateau from [[Nain, Newfoundland and Labrador|Nain]], NL to [[Kangiqsualujjuaq]], QC, with Todd McGowan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rcgs.org/programs/expeditions/2012_nunavik.asp|title=Trans-Nunavik expedition : 2012 Expeditions|website=www.rcgs.org|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-10-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019073846/http://www.rcgs.org/programs/expeditions/2012_nunavik.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* (2011) ''Boreal Heart'' : 25-day, 1120&nbsp;km journey by canoe through [[Ontario]]'s Little North from Pakashkan Lake to [[Peawanuck]], ON, with Todd McGowan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Westjet inflight magazine UP! feature "Tales of a Double Dipper"|url=http://cdn1.upmagazine.com/up-digital-issues/july2012/index.html|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019043621/http://cdn1.upmagazine.com/up-digital-issues/july2012/index.html|archive-date=2013-10-19|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* (2010) ''On the Line'' : 53-day, 2400&nbsp;km by bike, foot, pack raft, and kayak investigating the proposed [[Enbridge Northern Gateway Pipelines]] project, with Todd McGowan.<ref>{{cite news|title=Interview on CBC's "The Current"|url=http://www.cbc.ca/thecurrent/episode/2011/09/28/northern-gateway-pipeline/|work=CBC News|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-10-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021053856/http://www.cbc.ca/thecurrent/episode/2011/09/28/northern-gateway-pipeline/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2009) ''Mammalian'' : 46-day, 2004&nbsp;km journey by canoe through North America's largest wilderness from [[Yellowknife]] to [[Rankin Inlet]], with Taku Hokoyama.<ref>{{cite web|title=Feature article in UP! magazine "Exploring Yellowknife by Canoe"|url=http://www.upmagazine.com/story/article/exploring-yellowknife-canoe-w-video|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-10-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019043221/http://www.upmagazine.com/story/article/exploring-yellowknife-canoe-w-video|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2008) ''Bay or Bust'' : 25-day, 1050&nbsp;km journey by canoe from Opeongo Lake to [[Moosonee]], ON, with Alex Raymont.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://content.yudu.com/A12y8j/Canoerootsspring09/resources/39.htm|title=Canoeroots - Spring 2009|website=content.yudu.com|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-10-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018041215/http://content.yudu.com/A12y8j/Canoerootsspring09/resources/39.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2007) ''Borealis'' : 75-day, 3100&nbsp;km journey by canoe from [[Winnipeg]] to [[Parry Sound]] looking into the issues affecting the world's largest carbon bank- the [[Boreal Forest]] of [[Ontario]] and [[Manitoba]] with Taku Hokoyama.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rapidmedia.com/cr/canoerootsmag_fall08/|title=Canoeroots Magazine Cover Feature "On the Line"|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2014-01-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110125034/http://www.rapidmedia.com/cr/canoerootsmag_fall08/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2006) ''Sandakan Death March'' : Retracing of tragic WWII [[Sandakan Death March]] with Australian Military personnel, and Kevin Vallely.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.outpostmagazine.com/2013/02/25/sandakan-death-march/|title=Feature article in Outpost Magazine|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-10-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018010041/http://www.outpostmagazine.com/2013/02/25/sandakan-death-march/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2005) ''Shining Islands'' : 43-day, 900&nbsp;km kayak circumnavigation of the [[Haida Gwaii]] archipelago, with Keith Klapstein and Todd Macfie.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=http://content.yudu.com/A1re1x/akspring06/resources/35.htm|title=Adventure Kayak - Spring 2006|website=content.yudu.com|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-10-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018041437/http://content.yudu.com/A1re1x/akspring06/resources/35.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> 
* (2004) ''Across Asgaard'' : 26-day, 800&nbsp;km journey by canoe across [[Scandinavia]] from Bogden, [[Norway]] to [[Oulu]], [[Finland]], with Todd Macfie.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=amUqfdSp61c|title=Clip from CTV film "Across Asgaard"|website=[[YouTube]]|access-date=2016-11-29|archive-date=2016-04-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417064110/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=amUqfdSp61c|url-status=live}}</ref> 
* (2004) ''Taming the Motoco'' : 17-day journey by foot to the source of the Motoco River in [[Patagonia]] with a group of [[Argentinian]] explorers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fsR5PHvLjCE|title=Clip from CTV film "Taming the Motoco"|website=[[YouTube]]|access-date=2016-11-29|archive-date=2016-05-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160504011609/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fsR5PHvLjCE|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2003) ''Bikes on Ice'' : 49-day, 2000&nbsp;km journey by bike in winter on the [[Yukon River]] from [[Dawson City, Yukon|Dawson]] to [[Nome, Alaska|Nome]] retracing the route of two gold miners from 1901, with Kevin Vallely and Andy Sterns.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2003/05/0509_030509_bikesonice2.html|title=National Geographic Article|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2013-10-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019224238/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2003/05/0509_030509_bikesonice2.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* (2003) ''Nam Pha'' : 2nd descent of Nam Pha River in Laos in search of the Asian Water [[Tiger]], with Mick O'Shea and Brian Eustis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xlLBhK8F0z0|title=Clip from CTV film "Tiger Tracking on the Nam Pha"|website=[[YouTube]]|access-date=2016-11-29|archive-date=2014-03-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326085851/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xlLBhK8F0z0&app=desktop|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (2000) ''Phuket, Paddles, and Pirates'' : three-month sea kayaking/whitewater kayaking journey through [[Thailand]]/[[Malaysia]]/[[Indonesia]], with David Stibbe.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.readersdigest.ca/culture/choose-your-own-misadventure-when-wilderness-expeditions-take-wrong-turn/|title=Choose Your Own Misadventure: When Wilderness Expeditions Take a Wrong Turn|date=2 December 2021|access-date=27 August 2020|archive-date=20 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020090630/https://www.readersdigest.ca/culture/choose-your-own-misadventure-when-wilderness-expeditions-take-wrong-turn/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* (1998) ''Canadian Quest'' : 35-day, 1500&nbsp;km journey by canoe from [[Prince Rupert, British Columbia|Prince Rupert]] to Carcajou, with Ben O'Hara.<ref>{{cite web|title= Canadian Geographic Magazine article|url=http://business.highbeam.com/411060/article-1G1-20773348/one-stroke-time-rcgs-sponsors-canadian-quest-98-9300kilometre|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018015552/http://business.highbeam.com/411060/article-1G1-20773348/one-stroke-time-rcgs-sponsors-canadian-quest-98-9300kilometre|via= [[HighBeam Research]]|url-access= subscription|url-status=usurped|archive-date=2013-10-18}}</ref>
* (1995) ''C2C'' : 171-day, 8000&nbsp;km journey by canoe across Canada from [[Saint John, New Brunswick|Saint John]], NB to [[Vancouver]], BC, with Roman Rockliffe.<ref>{{cite web|title=Article on Clipper Canoes website|url=http://www.clippercanoes.com/c2c.php|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018012340/http://www.clippercanoes.com/c2c.php|archive-date=2013-10-18|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Writing==

Wolf is a regular feature writer, blogger, and photographer<ref>{{cite web|title=Explore Magazine blog|url=https://www.explore-mag.com/member.php?id=468378|access-date=2017-06-08|archive-date=2017-01-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170129121455/http://www.explore-mag.com/member.php?id=468378|url-status=live}},</ref> for [[Explore (magazine)|''Explore'']],<ref>{{cite web|title=Explore Magazine Article 'In the Land of Hairy Beasts'|website=[[Facebook]]|url=https://www.facebook.com/frank.wolf.3914/posts/10153229981401319?pnref=story|access-date=2016-01-27|archive-date=2023-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423171727/https://www.facebook.com/login/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Ffrank.wolf.3914%2Fposts%2F10153229981401319%3Fpnref%3Dstory|url-status=live}},</ref> and has written dozens of features for other publications including ''Mountain Life'',<ref>{{cite web|title= Mountain Life Magazine feature 'Ancient and Modern'|date= 16 December 2018|url= https://www.mountainlifemedia.ca/2018/12/ancient-modern-baffin-island-sea-to-frozen-sea/|access-date= 15 January 2019|archive-date= 15 January 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190115132449/https://www.mountainlifemedia.ca/2018/12/ancient-modern-baffin-island-sea-to-frozen-sea/|url-status= live}},</ref> ''Coast Mountain Culture'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BrBlEpahvLS/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/BrBlEpahvLS |archive-date=2021-12-26 |url-access=registration|title=Frank Wolf on Instagram: "A nice little two-pager I put together for the latest issue of @coastmountainculture magazine #canoe #adventure #nunavut @mec @esquifcanoes…"|website=Instagram}}{{cbignore}}</ref> ''Westjet'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.westjetmagazine.com/story/article/satisfy-need-adventure-canoe-trip-northern-ontario|title=Satisfy the need for adventure with a canoe trip in Northern Ontario|date=July 17, 2012|access-date=August 27, 2020|archive-date=January 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116000043/https://www.westjetmagazine.com/story/article/satisfy-need-adventure-canoe-trip-northern-ontario|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Canoeroots'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rapidmedia.com/cr/canoerootsmag_spring12/|title=Feature article in Canoeroots magazine "Frank Wolf's Dirty Little Secret"|access-date=2013-10-17|archive-date=2014-01-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110123759/http://www.rapidmedia.com/cr/canoerootsmag_spring12/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Reader's Digest]]'',<ref name="auto"/> ''Action Asia'', ''Adventure Kayak'',<ref name="auto1"/> ''Paddler'', ''Wend'', and ''[[The Province]]''. He has written two books: [[Lines on a Map (book)|''Lines on a Map'']], (2018) <ref>{{cite book|title=Lines on a Map book on Amazon|id={{ASIN|1771602899|country=ca}} }}</ref><ref name="auto2"/> and [[Two Springs, One Summer (book)|''Two Springs, One Summer'']] (2024)<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.cbc.ca/books/two-springs-one-summer-by-frank-wolf-1.7295416|title= CBC Review Two Springs, One Summer}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url= https://rmbooks.com/products/two-springs-one-summer|title= Two Springs, One Summer, RMB}}</ref>, both published by Rocky Mountain Books (RMB).

== Films ==
* ''Wild Ones'' (2017 film);<ref>{{cite web|title=Wild Ones film review in 'The Westender'|url=http://www.westender.com/arts-culture/reel-people/musician-and-filmmaker-tour-the-country-by-canoe-in-wild-ones-1.9715182|access-date=2017-08-30|archive-date=2017-08-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831044735/http://www.westender.com/arts-culture/reel-people/musician-and-filmmaker-tour-the-country-by-canoe-in-wild-ones-1.9715182|url-status=live}}</ref> Winner for 'Best Musical Adventure', 2017 Waterwalker Film Festival,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.paddlecanada.com/waterwalker-film-festival-winners/|title=2017 Waterwalker Film Winners|access-date=2017-08-30|archive-date=2017-08-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831050530/https://www.paddlecanada.com/waterwalker-film-festival-winners/|url-status=live}}</ref> Official Selection of 2017 Vancouver International Mountain Film Festival,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vimff.org/films/wild-ones/|title=VIMFF Wild Ones|access-date=2017-08-30|archive-date=2017-08-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831083237/https://vimff.org/films/wild-ones/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* [[The Hand of Franklin (Film)|''The Hand of Franklin'']] (2015 film); Winner for 'Best Documentary Feature' at the 2016 Ramunas Atelier International Film Awards,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ramuno-atelje.lt/index.php/raiifa|title=RAIIFA|website=www.ramuno-atelje.lt|access-date=2016-11-07|archive-date=2016-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161105201554/http://ramuno-atelje.lt/index.php/raiifa|url-status=live}}</ref> Winner for Best Canadian Film at 2015 Vancouver International Mountain Film Festival;<ref>{{cite web|title=VIMFF film awards 2015|url=http://www.vimff.org/films/vimff_film_awards_2015/|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150225035312/http://www.vimff.org/films/vimff_film_awards_2015/|archivedate=2015-02-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.explore-mag.com/The_Happy_Camper_Frank_Wolfs_new_film_The_Hand_of_Franklin|title=Explore Magazine|first=Kevin Hinton & Ryan|last=Mckenzie|website=Explore Magazine|access-date=2020-08-27|archive-date=2018-07-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715094225/https://www.explore-mag.com/The_Happy_Camper_Frank_Wolfs_new_film_The_Hand_of_Franklin|url-status=live}}</ref> Winner of the 'Adventure Award' at the 2016 [[San Francisco International Ocean Film Festival]];<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oceanfilmfest.org/news/2016/2/12/2016-awards|title=SFIOFF Award Winners|access-date=2016-02-19|archive-date=2016-03-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309130821/http://oceanfilmfest.org/news/2016/2/12/2016-awards|url-status=live}}</ref>
* [[Kitturiaq (2013 film)|''Kitturiaq'']] (2013 film); Winner for Best Adventure Film and Best Filmmaker at 2014 Waterwalker Film Festival;<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.paddlecanada.com/waterwalker-film-festival/1067-waterwalker-film-festival-winners.html|title=2014 Waterwalker Film Festival Winners|access-date=2014-03-06|archive-date=2014-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307004621/http://www.paddlecanada.com/waterwalker-film-festival/1067-waterwalker-film-festival-winners.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Kitturiaq Interview;<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.canoekayak.com/canoe/hard-line/#7d1c16bc80|title=Canoe&Kayak Magazine Interview with Frank Wolf|access-date=2014-03-06|archive-date=2014-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307000834/http://www.canoekayak.com/canoe/hard-line/#7d1c16bc80|url-status=live}}</ref> Kitturiaq Film Review;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.explore-mag.com/The_Happy_Camper_Kitturiaq_Film_Review|title=Explore Magazine|first=Kevin Hinton & Ryan|last=Mckenzie|website=Explore Magazine|access-date=2020-08-27|archive-date=2021-10-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020002259/https://www.explore-mag.com/The_Happy_Camper_Kitturiaq_Film_Review|url-status=live}}</ref>
* [[On the Line (2011 film)|''On the Line'']] (2011 film); Winner of the 'Spirit of Action Prize' at the 2012 Santa Cruz Film Festival';<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://santacruz.festivalgenius.com/2012/films/ontheline_frankwolf_santacruz2012|title=On The Line at SCFF|access-date=2012-11-09|archive-date=2013-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131117040252/http://santacruz.festivalgenius.com/2012/films/ontheline_frankwolf_santacruz2012|url-status=live}}</ref> Chosen for 'VIFF Selects' at the 2011 [[Vancouver International Film Festival]];
* [[Mammalian (2010 film)|''Mammalian'']] (2010 film); Top Ten most popular Canadian Films at the 2010 [[Vancouver International Film Festival]]; Winner of the 'Best Environment Film'<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ukclimbing.com/news/2011/11/kendal_mountain_festival_winners_2011-65099|title=Kendal Mountain Festival Winners 2011|website=www.ukclimbing.com|access-date=2020-08-27|archive-date=2023-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423171717/https://www.ukclimbing.com/news/2011/11/kendal_mountain_festival_winners_2011-65099|url-status=live}}</ref> at the 2011 [[Kendal Mountain Festival]]; Winner of the 2011 Reel Paddling Festival's "Best Canoeing Film";<ref>{{cite web|title=2011 RPFF Award Winning Films|url=http://www.reelpaddlingfilmfestival.com/films-mainmenu-35/winningfilms-mainmenu-81.html|access-date=2011-10-17|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201095542/http://www.reelpaddlingfilmfestival.com/films-mainmenu-35/winningfilms-mainmenu-81.html|archive-date=2013-02-01|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[Borealis (2008 film)|''Borealis'']] (2008 film); Winner of Grand Prize and Best Canadian Film at 2009 Vancouver International Mountain Film Festival;<ref>{{cite web|title=Borealis the Grand Prize Winner at 2009 VIMFF |url=http://www.vimff.org/archive/www.vimff.org/pages29ded.html?portalid=2&pageid=22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726002706/http://www.vimff.org/archive/www.vimff.org/pages29ded.html?portalid=2&pageid=22 |archivedate=2014-07-26 }}</ref>
* ''Exhibit Eh!'' (2007 TV series) <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.frank-wolf.net/p/exhibit-eh.html|title=Exhibit Eh! segment clips|access-date=2016-03-30|archive-date=2016-03-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160328230159/http://www.frank-wolf.net/p/exhibit-eh.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
* ''X-Quest'' (2004-2006 TV series) <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://frank-wolf.net/the-best-age-for-sex-have-you-peaked/|title=The Best Age for Sex: Have You Peaked? – Frank Wolf|website=frank-wolf.net|access-date=2020-08-27|archive-date=2020-08-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812142326/http://frank-wolf.net/the-best-age-for-sex-have-you-peaked/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Public speaking==

Wolf has given talks about his adventures and environmental work at [[TED (conference)|TEDx]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FVFjrf1OEY|title=TEDx talk about Frank's work as an Adventure Filmmaker|website=[[YouTube]]|access-date=2016-12-22|archive-date=2021-05-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522101647/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8FVFjrf1OEY|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmSHvB35Jkg&t=15s|title=TEDx talk about Frank's journey along the proposed route of the Northern Gateway Pipeline|website=[[YouTube]]|access-date=2018-08-17|archive-date=2023-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423171739/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmSHvB35Jkg&t=15s|url-status=live}}</ref> FEAT,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D2LZNILsjic|title=FEAT talk about Wolf's work (humorous)|website=[[YouTube]]|access-date=2016-12-22|archive-date=2017-01-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170121111708/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D2LZNILsjic|url-status=live}}</ref> and numerous other events.
